newsitem.title: UK: N. Sea crudes weaker with IPE but dated Brent firm.
newsitem.headline: N. Sea crudes weaker with IPE but dated Brent firm.

text.p: North Sea crude spot and paper prices were slightly weaker with futures, the exception being dated Brent which was supported by tightening early December supplies and fairly good demand, traders said.

"There's good interest for Dec cargoes, I think people are looking to square up early for the Christmas holiday season," another added. Despite one trader being five o'clocked on today's wet Brents, the keeping of a two early December cargoes and trade for a Dec 10-12 cargo at Jan +15 cents left dated Brent discounts slightly narrower at around 20-30 cents under December paper a gain of around 10 cents from Friday.

Traders said the market had largely ignored the volatility of the IPE but the forward paper contango had softened a little to reflect some of the futures market losses agtainst the possibilty of Iraqi crude sales, although most felt this would be easily absorbed.

CFDs however continued to indicated steady prompt sentiment after Friday's flurry of trade left the prompt market looking tight and saw differentials to dated Brent for other North Sea grades improving slightly.
"The market was picked clean last week but there still some good buying interest," one trader said.

A Gullfaks C loading Dec 12-14 traded on Monday at a stronger Dated Brent +34 cents and a Dec 13 loading Forties cargoe moved at a firm Dated Brent -27 cents to a French refiner. Balance of first decade December Ekofisk cargoes are now thought cleared with the last cargo sold by a French major at dated Brent +9 cents for Dec 6 loading.
A second decade cargo was heared traded at Dated Brent +23 cents.
Mediterranean refiners were slow to come out to buy crude on Monday following the strong differentials seen traded on Urals on Friday.
